attempts.rationale: Trend dominated, moderate seasonality, and the diagnostics suggest a weighted combination; test weighted inverse_error over the full pool.
The series has strong trend and moderate seasonality; a trimmed mean might reduce influence of outlier models.
Try a weighted combination with softmax_neg_error to see if a different weighting scheme improves over inverse_error, given moderate ranking stability and strong trend.
test a simple mean combination to see if removing weighting improves stability given moderate ranking tau and strong trend.

Test a weighted combination using the inverse_error scheme (w1) to see if a pure error‑based weighting outperforms the softmax variant; this explores a different weighting method while keeping the same pool.
Test a per‑horizon weighted combination using the top‑k mean per horizon (model cluster 4 dominates); this may capture horizon‑specific strengths.

The series has a strong trend and moderate seasonality; ranking stability is moderate, so a weighted combination that adapts to recent errors might help. I will test a DBA (data‑aware) approach to see if it can outperform the current weighted softmax.
Test a weighted combination that uses per‑horizon best models, leveraging the moderate ranking tau and strong trend where different models may dominate at different horizons.
The series has strong trend and moderate seasonality; a simple median might reduce influence of outlier models and could outperform weighted schemes when rankings are moderate.
The series has moderate ranking tau and strong trend; a per‑horizon weighted scheme that adapts to models whose errors are trending up or down may capture complementary strengths.
Test a tighter trimmed mean (trim_pct=0.1) to see if excluding extreme outlier models improves over median, given strong trend and moderate ranking stability.
The series has strong trend and moderate seasonality; a weighted combination using a forward‑selection weight (capturing complementary models) may improve over the current leader.
